We provide an analysis of the data, define the CRF-filling task and metric for its evaluation, and report on pilot experiments where we use an open-source state-of-the-art LLM to automatically execute the task. Results of the case-study show that (i) CRF-filling from real clinical notes in Italian can be approached in a zero-shot setting; (ii) LLMs' results are affected by biases (e.g., a cautious behaviour favours "unknown" answers), which need to be corrected.

AI.tldr: This paper introduces a new Italian Emergency Department clinical notes dataset annotated for CRF-filling, demonstrates zero-shot LLM performance on the task, and identifies biases in LLM responses that require correction.
AI.motivation: There is growing interest in automatic CRF-filling from clinical notes using LLMs, but progress is limited by scarcity of annotated CRF data for both training and testing models.
AI.method: Created a new dataset of Italian Emergency Department clinical notes annotated against a predefined CRF with 134 items. Defined the CRF-filling task and evaluation metrics, then conducted pilot experiments using an open-source state-of-the-art LLM in a zero-shot setting.
AI.result: The case study shows that (i) CRF-filling from real Italian clinical notes can be approached in zero-shot settings, and (ii) LLM results exhibit biases (e.g., cautious behavior favoring "unknown" answers) that need correction.
AI.conclusion: The paper provides a valuable annotated dataset for CRF-filling research and demonstrates both the feasibility of zero-shot approaches and the importance of addressing LLM biases in clinical information extraction tasks.

title: Quantity Convergence, Quality Divergence: Disentangling Fluency and Accuracy in L2 Mandarin Prosody
summary: While second language (L2) learners may acquire target syntactic word order, mapping this syntax onto appropriate prosodic structures remains a persistent challenge. This study investigates the fossilization and stability of the L2 syntax-prosody interface by comparing 67 native Mandarin speakers with 67 Vietnamese learners using the BLCU-SAIT corpus. By integrating C-ToBI boundary annotation with Dependency Grammar analysis, we examined both the quantity of prosodic boundaries and their mapping to syntactic relations. Results reveal a non-linear acquisition: although high-proficiency learners (VNH) converge to the native baseline in boundary quantity at the Major Phrase level (B3), their structural mapping significantly diverges. Specifically, VNH demote the prosodic boundary at the Subject-Verb (SBV) interface (Major Phrase B3 -> Prosodic Word B1), while erroneously promoting the boundary at the Verb-Object (VOB) interface (Prosodic Word B1 -> Major Phrase B3). This strategy allows learners to maintain high long phrasal output at the expense of structural accuracy. This results in a distorted prosodic hierarchy where the native pattern is inverted.

AI.tldr: L2 learners acquire target syntactic word order but struggle with mapping syntax to prosodic structures, showing fossilization at the syntax-prosody interface with non-linear acquisition patterns.
AI.motivation: To investigate the fossilization and stability of the L2 syntax-prosody interface, examining how learners map acquired syntactic structures onto appropriate prosodic boundaries despite persistent challenges in this domain.
AI.method: Comparative study of 67 native Mandarin speakers and 67 Vietnamese learners using the BLCU-SAIT corpus, integrating C-ToBI boundary annotation with Dependency Grammar analysis to examine both prosodic boundary quantity and their mapping to syntactic relations.
AI.result: High-proficiency learners converge to native baseline in boundary quantity at Major Phrase level (B3) but show significant divergence in structural mapping: they demote prosodic boundaries at Subject-Verb interface (B3→B1) while erroneously promoting boundaries at Verb-Object interface (B1→B3), creating an inverted prosodic hierarchy.
AI.conclusion: L2 learners develop a compensatory strategy that maintains high phrasal output at the expense of structural accuracy, resulting in fossilized, distorted prosodic hierarchies that invert native patterns, demonstrating persistent challenges at the syntax-prosody interface.

title: CiteLLM: An Agentic Platform for Trustworthy Scientific Reference Discovery
summary: Large language models (LLMs) have created new opportunities to enhance the efficiency of scholarly activities; however, challenges persist in the ethical deployment of AI assistance, including (1) the trustworthiness of AI-generated content, (2) preservation of academic integrity and intellectual property, and (3) protection of information privacy. In this work, we present CiteLLM, a specialized agentic platform designed to enable trustworthy reference discovery for grounding author-drafted claims and statements. The system introduces a novel interaction paradigm by embedding LLM utilities directly within the LaTeX editor environment, ensuring a seamless user experience and no data transmission outside the local system. To guarantee hallucination-free references, we employ dynamic discipline-aware routing to retrieve candidates exclusively from trusted web-based academic repositories, while leveraging LLMs solely for generating context-aware search queries, ranking candidates by relevance, and validating and explaining support through paragraph-level semantic matching and an integrated chatbot. Evaluation results demonstrate the superior performance of the proposed system in returning valid and highly usable references.

AI.tldr: CiteLLM is a specialized AI platform integrated into LaTeX editors that provides trustworthy reference discovery by routing searches to academic repositories while using LLMs only for query generation and ranking, ensuring no hallucinations and local data privacy.
AI.motivation: LLMs enhance scholarly efficiency but face ethical challenges: (1) trustworthiness of AI-generated content, (2) preservation of academic integrity and intellectual property, and (3) protection of information privacy.
AI.method: CiteLLM embeds LLM utilities directly within LaTeX editors with local-only data processing. It uses dynamic discipline-aware routing to retrieve candidates exclusively from trusted academic repositories. LLMs are limited to generating context-aware search queries, ranking candidates by relevance, and validating support through paragraph-level semantic matching with an integrated chatbot.
AI.result: Evaluation demonstrates superior performance in returning valid and highly usable references compared to existing approaches.
AI.conclusion: CiteLLM provides a trustworthy reference discovery solution that addresses ethical concerns in AI-assisted scholarly work by preventing hallucinations, preserving academic integrity, and ensuring data privacy through local processing and repository-based retrieval.

title: Assessing Deanonymization Risks with Stylometry-Assisted LLM Agent
summary: The rapid advancement of large language models (LLMs) has enabled powerful authorship inference capabilities, raising growing concerns about unintended deanonymization risks in textual data such as news articles. In this work, we introduce an LLM agent designed to evaluate and mitigate such risks through a structured, interpretable pipeline. Central to our framework is the proposed $\textit{SALA}$ (Stylometry-Assisted LLM Analysis) method, which integrates quantitative stylometric features with LLM reasoning for robust and transparent authorship attribution. Experiments on large-scale news datasets demonstrate that $\textit{SALA}$, particularly when augmented with a database module, achieves high inference accuracy in various scenarios. Finally, we propose a guided recomposition strategy that leverages the agent's reasoning trace to generate rewriting prompts, effectively reducing authorship identifiability while preserving textual meaning. Our findings highlight both the deanonymization potential of LLM agents and the importance of interpretable, proactive defenses for safeguarding author privacy.

AI.tldr: SALA framework combines stylometric features with LLM reasoning for authorship attribution and privacy protection through guided recomposition.
AI.motivation: Address growing concerns about unintended deanonymization risks in textual data due to LLMs' powerful authorship inference capabilities.
AI.method: SALA (Stylometry-Assisted LLM Analysis) integrates quantitative stylometric features with LLM reasoning in a structured pipeline, augmented with database module and guided recomposition strategy.
AI.result: SALA achieves high inference accuracy on large-scale news datasets, particularly when augmented with database module; guided recomposition effectively reduces authorship identifiability while preserving textual meaning.
AI.conclusion: Highlights both deanonymization potential of LLM agents and importance of interpretable, proactive defenses for safeguarding author privacy.

title: From Blind Spots to Gains: Diagnostic-Driven Iterative Training for Large Multimodal Models
summary: As Large Multimodal Models (LMMs) scale up and reinforcement learning (RL) methods mature, LMMs have made notable progress in complex reasoning and decision making. Yet training still relies on static data and fixed recipes, making it difficult to diagnose capability blind spots or provide dynamic, targeted reinforcement. Motivated by findings that test driven error exposure and feedback based correction outperform repetitive practice, we propose Diagnostic-driven Progressive Evolution (DPE), a spiral loop where diagnosis steers data generation and reinforcement, and each iteration re-diagnoses the updated model to drive the next round of targeted improvement. DPE has two key components. First, multiple agents annotate and quality control massive unlabeled multimodal data, using tools such as web search and image editing to produce diverse, realistic samples. Second, DPE attributes failures to specific weaknesses, dynamically adjusts the data mixture, and guides agents to generate weakness focused data for targeted reinforcement. Experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct show stable, continual gains across eleven benchmarks, indicating DPE as a scalable paradigm for continual LMM training under open task distributions. Our code, models, and data are publicly available at https://github.com/hongruijia/DPE.

AI.tldr: DPE (Diagnostic-driven Progressive Evolution) is a spiral training loop for Large Multimodal Models that uses diagnosis to steer data generation and reinforcement learning, enabling targeted improvement through iterative error analysis and weakness-focused data creation.
AI.motivation: Current LMM training relies on static data and fixed recipes, making it difficult to diagnose capability blind spots or provide dynamic, targeted reinforcement. The authors are motivated by findings that test-driven error exposure and feedback-based correction outperform repetitive practice.
AI.method: DPE consists of two key components: 1) Multiple agents annotate and quality control massive unlabeled multimodal data using tools like web search and image editing to produce diverse, realistic samples; 2) DPE attributes failures to specific weaknesses, dynamically adjusts the data mixture, and guides agents to generate weakness-focused data for targeted reinforcement.
AI.result: Experiments on Qwen3-VL-8B-Instruct and Qwen2.5-VL-7B-Instruct show stable, continual gains across eleven benchmarks, indicating DPE as a scalable paradigm for continual LMM training under open task distributions.
AI.conclusion: DPE represents a scalable paradigm for continual LMM training that enables targeted improvement through diagnostic-driven data generation and reinforcement, addressing limitations of static training approaches.

title: GeoWorld: Geometric World Models
summary: Energy-based predictive world models provide a powerful approach for multi-step visual planning by reasoning over latent energy landscapes rather than generating pixels. However, existing approaches face two major challenges: (i) their latent representations are typically learned in Euclidean space, neglecting the underlying geometric and hierarchical structure among states, and (ii) they struggle with long-horizon prediction, which leads to rapid degradation across extended rollouts. To address these challenges, we introduce GeoWorld, a geometric world model that preserves geometric structure and hierarchical relations through a Hyperbolic JEPA, which maps latent representations from Euclidean space onto hyperbolic manifolds. We further introduce Geometric Reinforcement Learning for energy-based optimization, enabling stable multi-step planning in hyperbolic latent space. Extensive experiments on CrossTask and COIN demonstrate around 3% SR improvement in 3-step planning and 2% SR improvement in 4-step planning compared to the state-of-the-art V-JEPA 2. Project website: https://steve-zeyu-zhang.github.io/GeoWorld.

AI.tldr: GeoWorld introduces a hyperbolic geometric world model that preserves hierarchical structure for improved long-horizon visual planning, achieving 3% SR improvement over V-JEPA 2.
AI.motivation: Existing energy-based predictive world models have two key limitations: (1) they use Euclidean latent spaces that neglect geometric and hierarchical structure among states, and (2) they struggle with long-horizon prediction leading to rapid degradation in extended rollouts.
AI.method: GeoWorld introduces a Hyperbolic JEPA (Joint Embedding Predictive Architecture) that maps latent representations from Euclidean space onto hyperbolic manifolds to preserve geometric structure and hierarchical relations. It also uses Geometric Reinforcement Learning for energy-based optimization to enable stable multi-step planning in hyperbolic latent space.
AI.result: Extensive experiments on CrossTask and COIN datasets demonstrate approximately 3% success rate (SR) improvement in 3-step planning and 2% SR improvement in 4-step planning compared to state-of-the-art V-JEPA 2.
AI.conclusion: GeoWorld successfully addresses the limitations of existing energy-based world models by incorporating hyperbolic geometry to preserve structural relationships, enabling more stable and effective long-horizon visual planning.

title: Retrieve and Segment: Are a Few Examples Enough to Bridge the Supervision Gap in Open-Vocabulary Segmentation?
summary: Open-vocabulary segmentation (OVS) extends the zero-shot recognition capabilities of vision-language models (VLMs) to pixel-level prediction, enabling segmentation of arbitrary categories specified by text prompts. Despite recent progress, OVS lags behind fully supervised approaches due to two challenges: the coarse image-level supervision used to train VLMs and the semantic ambiguity of natural language. We address these limitations by introducing a few-shot setting that augments textual prompts with a support set of pixel-annotated images. Building on this, we propose a retrieval-augmented test-time adapter that learns a lightweight, per-image classifier by fusing textual and visual support features. Unlike prior methods relying on late, hand-crafted fusion, our approach performs learned, per-query fusion, achieving stronger synergy between modalities. The method supports continually expanding support sets, and applies to fine-grained tasks such as personalized segmentation. Experiments show that we significantly narrow the gap between zero-shot and supervised segmentation while preserving open-vocabulary ability.

AI.tldr: Retrieval-augmented test-time adapter for open-vocabulary segmentation using few-shot visual support to improve zero-shot performance and reduce gap with supervised methods.
AI.motivation: Open-vocabulary segmentation lags behind supervised approaches due to coarse image-level supervision in VLMs and semantic ambiguity of natural language prompts.
AI.method: Introduces few-shot setting with pixel-annotated support images and proposes retrieval-augmented test-time adapter that learns lightweight per-image classifier by fusing textual and visual support features through learned, per-query fusion.
AI.result: Significantly narrows gap between zero-shot and supervised segmentation while preserving open-vocabulary ability; supports continually expanding support sets and fine-grained tasks like personalized segmentation.
AI.conclusion: The proposed approach effectively addresses limitations of current OVS methods by combining textual prompts with visual support, achieving stronger modality synergy and improved performance.

title: MediX-R1: Open Ended Medical Reinforcement Learning
summary: We introduce MediX-R1, an open-ended Reinforcement Learning (RL) framework for medical multimodal large language models (MLLMs) that enables clinically grounded, free-form answers beyond multiple-choice formats. MediX-R1 fine-tunes a baseline vision-language backbone with Group Based RL and a composite reward tailored for medical reasoning: an LLM-based accuracy reward that judges semantic correctness with a strict YES/NO decision, a medical embedding-based semantic reward to capture paraphrases and terminology variants, and lightweight format and modality rewards that enforce interpretable reasoning and modality recognition. This multi-signal design provides stable, informative feedback for open-ended outputs where traditional verifiable or MCQ-only rewards fall short. To measure progress, we propose a unified evaluation framework for both text-only and image+text tasks that uses a Reference-based LLM-as-judge in place of brittle string-overlap metrics, capturing semantic correctness, reasoning, and contextual alignment. Despite using only $\sim51$K instruction examples, MediX-R1 achieves excellent results across standard medical LLM (text-only) and VLM (image + text) benchmarks, outperforming strong open-source baselines and delivering particularly large gains on open-ended clinical tasks. Our results demonstrate that open-ended RL with comprehensive reward signals and LLM-based evaluation is a practical path toward reliable medical reasoning in multimodal models. Our trained models, curated datasets and source code are available at https://medix.cvmbzuai.com

AI.tldr: MediX-R1 is an open-ended RL framework for medical MLLMs that uses composite rewards (LLM-based accuracy, medical embedding semantics, format/modality) to enable clinically grounded free-form answers beyond multiple-choice formats, achieving strong performance across medical benchmarks with only ~51K examples.
AI.motivation: Current medical MLLMs are limited to multiple-choice formats and lack open-ended reasoning capabilities. Traditional RL approaches struggle with free-form medical answers where verifiable or MCQ-only rewards are insufficient for evaluating semantic correctness and clinical reasoning.
AI.method: Fine-tunes a baseline vision-language backbone using Group Based RL with a composite reward: 1) LLM-based accuracy reward for semantic correctness with YES/NO decisions, 2) medical embedding-based semantic reward for capturing paraphrases and terminology variants, 3) lightweight format and modality rewards for interpretable reasoning and modality recognition. Uses Reference-based LLM-as-judge evaluation framework.
AI.result: Achieves excellent results across standard medical LLM (text-only) and VLM (image+text) benchmarks, outperforming strong open-source baselines. Shows particularly large gains on open-ended clinical tasks despite using only ~51K instruction examples.
AI.conclusion: Open-ended RL with comprehensive reward signals and LLM-based evaluation is a practical path toward reliable medical reasoning in multimodal models. The framework enables clinically grounded, free-form answers beyond traditional multiple-choice limitations.
